PSYC 100.title: Introductory Psychology
PSYC 100.description: Introduction to methods and statistics, biopsychology, learning, perception, memory, cognition, motivation, assessment, developmental, personality, clinical, and social psychology.

PSYC 101.title: Introduction to Biological and Cognitive Psychology
PSYC 101.description: Introduction to Methods and Statistics, Biopsychology, Learning, Perception, Memory, and Cognition.

PSYC 102.title: Introduction to Developmental, Social, Personality, and Clinical Psychology
PSYC 102.description: Introduction to methods and statistics, motivation, assessment, developmental, personality, clinical, and social psychology.

PSYC 203.title: Career Exploration using Psychology
PSYC 203.description: Critical application of psychological concepts to further personal growth. Methods and strategies for exploring careers as a process that unfolds across the lifespan.

PSYC 207.title: Contemporary Topics in Biological and Cognitive Psychology
PSYC 207.description: A focus on the interpretation of contemporary research in neuroscience, cognition, perception, memory, and learning.

PSYC 208.title: Contemporary Topics in Social, Developmental, Personality, and Clinical Psychology
PSYC 208.description: A focus on the interpretation of contemporary research in social, developmental, personality, and clinical psychology.

PSYC 216.title: Questioning Psychological Science in the Media
PSYC 216.description: Use basic principles of quantitative psychological research methods to critique psychological claims presented in the media and to translate psychological science to everyday life. Intended for non-psychology majors to prepare for upper level courses. Majors should take PSYC 217 instead.

PSYC 217.title: Research Methods
PSYC 217.description: Focus on various research methods used in psychology, with an emphasis on critical thinking and experimental design. Restricted to students in one of PSYC Major, BA COGS Major.
PSYC 217.corequisiteText: Either (a) PSYC_V 100 or (b) all of PSYC 101 or PSYO_O 111, PSYC_V 102 or PSYO_O 121

PSYC 218.title: Analysis of Behavioural Data
PSYC 218.description: Use of inferential statistics in psychology and conceptual interpretation of data; experimental design (laboratory, field research methods); presentation of data analyses in reports. Restricted to students in one of PSYC Major, BA COGS Major.

PSYC 240.title: Research Experience
PSYC 240.description: Applied research experience in an active psychology research lab. See Psychology Department website for application.

PSYC 277.title: Behavioural and Neuroscientific Research Methods
PSYC 277.description: Research methods used in the neurosciences. Restricted to students in one of NSCI Major, BSc COGS Major (Cognition and Brain stream).

PSYC 278.title: Analysis of Behavioural and Neuroscientific Data
PSYC 278.description: Statistical methods for use in the neurosciences. Restricted to students in one of NSCI Major, BSc COGS Major (Cognition and Brain stream).

PSYC 300.title: Introduction to Psychopathology and Clinical Science
PSYC 300.description: The definition, history, and scope of mental illness; emphasis on the psychological factors that control its origins, maintenance, and modification. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher. Strongly recommended: PSYC_V 101, 102, and one of PSYC_V 216, 217, or 227.

PSYC 301.title: Brain Dysfunction and Recovery
PSYC 301.description: Cognitive and behavioral impairments resulting from brain dysfunction. Focus on the efficacy of various intervention approaches. Strongly recommended: PSYC 101, 102, and one of PSYC 216, PSYC 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

PSYC 302.title: Infancy
PSYC 302.description: Human cognition, perception, motor, social, emotional needs, brain development and their interactions from birth until the emergence of language. Strongly recommended: PSYC 101, 102, and one of PSYC 216, PSYC 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

PSYC 303.title: Tests and Measurements
PSYC 303.description: Theory and practice of psychological measurement, statistical models for items and tests, assessment of test reliability and validity, factor analysis, scoring. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

PSYC 305.title: Personality Psychology
PSYC 305.description: Theory and research on individual differences in motivation, emotion, and social behaviour. Strongly recommended: PSYC 102, and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

PSYC 306.title: Principles of Animal Behaviour
PSYC 306.description: Behavioural neuroscience; behavioural genetics; social systems; mating and parental strategies; instinct and learning; evolution of human behaviour. Strongly recommended: PSYC 101, and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

PSYC 307.title: Cultural Psychology
PSYC 307.description: Cultural influences on human thought and behaviour; interactions of culture and self; multicultural experiences; intercultural relations; methodological issues. Strongly recommended: PSYC 102, and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

PSYC 308.title: Social Psychology
PSYC 308.description: Theory and research of individual social behaviour; social motivation; attitudes; group interaction; socialization; prejudice. Strongly recommended: PSYC 102, and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

PSYC 309.title: Cognitive Processes
PSYC 309.description: Contribution of cognitive processes to perception, attention, and memory; cognitive development, language, thinking, and creativity. Strongly recommended: PSYC 101 and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

PSYC 311.title: Psychology of Sport
PSYC 311.description: Psychological theory, research, and skills training related to sport performance, exercise motivation, and adherence. Strongly recommended: PSYC 101 and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

PSYC 312.title: History of Psychology
PSYC 312.description: The principal trends of psychological explanation and events in the history of psychology from the earliest times to the present. Strongly recommended: PSYC 101 and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to Psychology Major or Psychology Honours students.

PSYC 314.title: Health Psychology
PSYC 314.description: Health-related behaviours such as smoking and drug use; effects of stressful events on health; methods for coping with stress; impact of chronic illness on the family; social support systems. Strongly recommended: PSYC 102 and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

PSYC 315.title: Childhood and Adolescence
PSYC 315.description: Human development from the preschool period through adolescence. Strongly recommended: PSYC 102 and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

PSYC 319.title: Applied Developmental Psychology
PSYC 319.description: Applications of theories and research in developmental psychology to contemporary social issues; topics may include daycare, child abuse, divorce and remarriage, substance abuse, sexuality. Strongly recommended: PSYC 102 and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

PSYC 320.title: Psychology of Sex Differences
PSYC 320.description: Theory and research on gender development and the influence of sex and/or gender on cognition, emotion, motivation, social behaviour, and health. Strongly recommended: PSYC 101, 102 and PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

PSYC 322.title: Adulthood and Aging
PSYC 322.description: Issues, theories, and psychological research regarding adulthood and the aging process. Strongly recommended: PSYC 102 and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

PSYC 324.title: Brain and Behavior (I)
PSYC 324.description: The neurobiological bases of behaviour (I); Neuroanatomy and neural communication, neuroscience research methods, brain processes involved in perception and movement. This course is strongly recommended for students who have taken PSYC_V 101 and one of PSYC_V 216, PSYC_V 217. Restricted to all Arts and Science students with second-year standing or higher, excluding those in the B.Sc. Neuroscience specializations.

PSYC 325.title: Socialization: Media Content and Effects
PSYC 325.description: Examines human development in the context of the socializing role of media. Strongly recommended: PSYC 102 and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

PSYC 331.title: Forensic Psychology
PSYC 331.description: The application of psychological theory and research to legal issues and the criminal justice system. Strongly recommended: PSYC 102 and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

PSYC 333.title: Memory: Historical, Clinical and Cognitive Perspectives
PSYC 333.description: Classical and contemporary metaphors for memory and their impact on theory development. Strongly recommended: PSYC 101 and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

PSYC 334.title: Memory II
PSYC 334.description: Organic amnesia; remembering childhood events; the self and memory; and the problem of distinguishing genuine from simulated forgetting.

PSYC 335.title: Gambling and Decision Making
PSYC 335.description: The psychology of gambling behaviour, with emphasis on relevant work from judgment and decision-making, the cognitive neuroscience of choice, and clinical perspectives on disordered gambling. Strongly recommended: PSYC 101 and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

PSYC 336.title: The Psychology of Language I
PSYC 336.description: Psychological abilities underlying human language; language processing, lexical representation, and principles of online conversation; animal versus human communication. Strongly recommended: PSYC 101 and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

PSYC 337.title: The Psychology of Language II
PSYC 337.description: Language and thought; deriving psychological principles from language universals; the psychology of literacy, dyslexia, multilingualism, and natural language processing.

PSYC 340.title: Directed Studies in Psychology
PSYC 340.description: Directed investigation of a research problem, requiring a written report of the findings. Requires the supervising faculty member's permission. See the Department's website for more information. Restricted to Majors in Psychology or Cognitive Systems with second-year standing or higher.

PSYC 344.title: Brain and Behavior (II)
PSYC 344.description: The neurobiological bases of behaviour (II); neural mechanisms underlying sexual behavior, feeding, sleep, motivation, emotion, learning and memory, psychopathology. Restricted to all Arts and Science students with second-year standing or higher, excluding those in the B.Sc. Neuroscience specializations.

PSYC 348.title: Honours Seminar I
PSYC 348.description: Orientation to psychological research, with special emphasis on ongoing research within the department; effective presentation of research findings, oral and written; critical evaluation of research. Requires a research project. Restricted to students in Honours Psychology.
PSYC 348.prerequisiteText: All of PSYC_V 217 or PSYO_O 270, PSYC_V 218 or PSYO_ 271

PSYC 349.title: Honours Seminar II
PSYC 349.description: Continuation of PSYC_V 349. Restricted to students in Honours Psychology.

PSYC 350.title: Psychological Aspects of Human Sexuality
PSYC 350.description: Human sexuality from a biopsychological, behavioural, and psychosocial perspective. Strongly recommended: PSYC 101, 102 and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

PSYC 358.title: Evolutionary Psychology
PSYC 358.description: Theory and research on the evolution of the human mind, with emphasis on implications for cognition and behaviour in contemporary environments. Strongly recommended: PSYC 102 and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

PSYC 359.title: Advanced Research Methods in Behavioural Sciences
PSYC 359.description: Prepares students for graduate studies or other advanced behavioural research; experimental design and analytic techniques; laboratory with computer applications. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher and a cumulative average at or above 76%.

PSYC 361.title: Neuroscience of Motivation
PSYC 361.description: Experimental analysis of hunger, thirst, exploratory and curiosity behaviour, maternal and reproductive behaviour, fixed action patterns, and complex processes involved in social motivation with emphasis on the biological basis of motivation. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.
PSYC 361.prerequisiteText: One of NSCI_V 201, PSYC_V 304, PSYC_V 344, PSYC_V 370

PSYC 363.title: Neuroscience of Simple Learning
PSYC 363.description: Introduction to basic theories of non-associative learning, classical and operant conditioning. Experimental findings from behavioural and biological analyses with animals and humans. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.
PSYC 363.prerequisiteText: One of PSYC_V 304, PSYC_V 324, BIOL_V 361, NSCI_V 200

PSYC 365.title: Cognitive Neuroscience
PSYC 365.description: Current research into human brain systems underlying cognitive processes such as perception, attention, memory, and decision-making. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.
PSYC 365.prerequisiteText: Either (a) one of PSYC_V 304, PSYC_V 309, PSYC_V 344, NSCI_V 201 or (b) COGS_V 200

PSYC 367.title: Sensory Systems
PSYC 367.description: Anatomy and physiology of the sensory pathways and their relation to perception. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.
PSYC 367.prerequisiteText: Either (a) one of PSYC 101, NSCI 201 or (b) COGS 200

PSYC 368.title: Perceptual Processing
PSYC 368.description: Perceptual phenomena and their underlying brain mechanisms.

PSYC 370.title: Behavioural and Cognitive Neuroscience I
PSYC 370.description: Advanced methods and topics in behavioural and cognitive neuroscience. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher who are in the Neuroscience Major or Honours or in the Cognitive Systems Major programs.

PSYC 371.title: Behavioural and Cognitive Neuroscience II
PSYC 371.description: Neurodevelopment and neuroplasticity, the physiological bases of several motivated behaviours (sleep, sexual behaviour, hunger and eating, drugs and addiction), cognition, the stress response, and brain dysfunction and recovery. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher who are in the Neuroscience Major or Honours or in the Cognitive Systems Major programs.

PSYC 388.title: Directed Studies in Behavioural Neuroscience
PSYC 388.description: Directed investigation of an experimental problem in Behavioural Neuroscience requiring a written report of the findings. Requires the supervising faculty member's permission. See the Department's website for more information. Restricted to Majors in PSYC or COGS or NSCI with second-year standing or higher.

PSYC 398.title: Cooperative Work Placement I
PSYC 398.description: Approved and supervised relevant work experience in an industrial, academic, or government setting for a minimum of 13 weeks, full-time. Normally taken in Summer Session after third year. Work term report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-op Program in Psychology.

PSYC 399.title: Cooperative Work Placement II
PSYC 399.description: Approved and supervised relevant work experience in an industrial, academic, or government setting for a minimum of 13 weeks, full-time. Normally taken in fourth year Winter Session, Term 1. Work term report required. Pass/Fail. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-op Program in Psychology.

PSYC 400.title: Clinical Psychology: A Health Profession
PSYC 400.description: Theory, research, practice, and professional issues in clinical psychology, including a practicum placement. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher.

PSYC 401.title: Clinical Psychology
PSYC 401.description: Theoretical and research foundations of the processes of assessment and behaviour modification in clinical psychology. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher. Strongly recommended: PSYC 217, PSYC 277 and PSYC 300.

PSYC 402.title: Research in Psychological Disorders
PSYC 402.description: Focus on the cognitive, biological, and motivational underpinnings of psychological disorders. Topics include current research methods, controversies in the research literature, and directions for future research. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher.

PSYC 403.title: Human Emotion
PSYC 403.description: Developmental, cognitive, and social psychological theories and research on human emotion. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher.
PSYC 403.prerequisiteText: One of PSYC 217, PSYC 277 and one of PSYC 305, PSYC 307, PSYC 308, PSYC 358

PSYC 404.title: Psychology of Religion
PSYC 404.description: Cognitive, emotional, and motivational underpinnings of religious behaviour; supernatural beliefs, magical thinking, ritual, sacrifice; religion's role in morality, prosociality, health, violence, and intergroup relations. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher.
PSYC 404.prerequisiteText: One of PSYC 217, PSYC 277 and one of PSYC 305, PSYC 307, PSYC 308, PSYC 358

PSYC 407.title: Cognition and Culture
PSYC 407.description: Cultural learning; cultural variation and universality in cognition and emotion; cognitive and emotional bases of cultural phenomena. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher.
PSYC 407.prerequisiteText: One of PSYC 217, PSYC 277 and one of PSYC 307, PSYC 308, PSYC 358

PSYC 408.title: Research in Social Psychology
PSYC 408.description: Representative studies on social psychological topics; emphasis on the formulation of significant questions and the design and execution of relevant research. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher.
PSYC 408.prerequisiteText: One of PSYC 217, PSYC 277 and one of PSYC 305, PSYC 307, PSYC 308, PSYC 358

PSYC 409.title: Cognitive Neuropsychology
PSYC 409.description: The structure of the mind as revealed by brain injury, neurological illness, and surgical intervention. Topics include attention, memory, language, sense of self, topographic awareness, moral reasoning, emotion, theory of mind, and social awareness. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher.
PSYC 409.prerequisiteText: Either (a) one of PSYC_V 304, PSYC_V 309, PSYC_V 344, NSCI_V 201 or (b) COGS_V 200

PSYC 412.title: Cognitive Development
PSYC 412.description: The development of fundamental cognitive abilities from infancy through adulthood, including traditional approaches to cognitive development as well as new areas of current investigation. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher.
PSYC 412.prerequisiteText: One of PSYC 217, PSYC 277 and one of PSYC 302, PSYC 315, PSYC 319, PSYC 322, PSYC 325

PSYC 413.title: Social and Personality Development
PSYC 413.description: Comprehensive overview of the psychological processes in the social and personality development of infants, children, and adolescents. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher. Strongly recommended: PSYC 217, PSYC 277 and one of PSYC 302, PSYC 315, PSYC 319, PSYC 322, PSYC 325.

PSYC 414.title: Research in Developmental Psychology
PSYC 414.description: Advanced study of current research in a specific area of developmental psychology. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher.
PSYC 414.prerequisiteText: One of PSYC 217, PSYC 277 and one of PSYC 302, PSYC 315, PSYC 319, PSYC 322, PSYC 325

PSYC 415.title: Applied Social Psychology
PSYC 415.description: The application of social psychological research and theory to the solution of social problems. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher.
PSYC 415.prerequisiteText: One of PSYC 217, PSYC 277 and one of PSYC 305, PSYC 307, PSYC 308, PSYC 358

PSYC 417.title: Special Topics in Psychology
PSYC 417.description: Intensive examination of selected topics and issues in psychology. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher.
PSYC 417.prerequisiteText: One of PSYC 217, PSYC 277 and one of PSYC 218, PSYC 278

PSYC 418.title: The Self-Concept
PSYC 418.description: Theory and research on the self: development, knowledge, motivation, emotions, presentation. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher.
PSYC 418.prerequisiteText: One of PSYC 217, PSYC 277 and one of PSYC 305, PSYC 307, PSYC 308, PSYC 358

PSYC 420.title: Community Psychology
PSYC 420.description: The relationships between social contexts and wellbeing with a focus on the application of psychology to disadvantaged populations and community development. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher.
PSYC 420.prerequisiteText: Either (a) one of PSYC 217, PSYC 277 and one of PSYC 300, PSYC 308, PSYC 314; or (b) PSYC 319

PSYC 421.title: Environmental Psychology
PSYC 421.description: Psychological theory and research on the interaction between organisms and the physical environment; emphasis on applications to the design and management of constructed and natural environments. Strongly recommended: PSYC 217, PSYC 277 and one of PSYC 300, PSYC 308, PSYC 309, PSYC 314, PSYC 319. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher.

PSYC 427.title: Advanced Seminar in Psychology
PSYC 427.description: Investigation of an issue, topic, or phenomenon in psychology, focusing on research deeply within a subfield or integrating research across subfields. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher.
PSYC 427.prerequisiteText: One of PSYC 217, PSYC 277 and one of PSYC 218, PSYC 278
notes: Consult Section Notes or the Psychology Department website for 300-level course(s) recommended for a specific offering.

PSYC 440.title: Directed Studies in Psychology
PSYC 440.description: Directed investigation of a research problem, requiring a written report of the findings. Requires the supervising faculty member's permission. See the Department's website for more information. Restricted to Majors in Psychology or Cognitive Systems, with third-year standing or higher.

PSYC 448.title: Honours Seminar III
PSYC 448.description: Students carry out a research project and report on its development during seminars. Discussion of research with emphasis on choice of problems, research design and data analysis. Restricted to students in Honours Psychology.

PSYC 449.title: Honours Seminar IV
PSYC 449.description: Continuation of PSYC_V 448. Restricted to students in Honours Psychology.

PSYC 460.title: Behavioural Neuroendocrinology
PSYC 460.description: Detailed examination of the interaction between hormones and neural control of reproductive and non-reproductive behaviours; emphasis on gonadal and adrenal hormone effects on learning and memory in the brain. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher.
PSYC 460.prerequisiteText: One of PSYC_V 304, PSYC_V 344, PSYC_V 371, BIOL_V 372

PSYC 461.title: Neuroplasticity and Behaviour
PSYC 461.description: Experimental findings and theory documenting the plasticity of the brain and its relationship to behaviour: emphasis on gene regulation, neurogenesis and cell morphology changes in relation to learning and experience. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher.
PSYC 461.prerequisiteText: One of PSYC_V 304, PSYC_V 344, PSYC_V 371, BIOL_V 372

PSYC 462.title: Drugs and Behavioural Neuroscience
PSYC 462.description: Introduction to neurochemical systems and functional neuroanatomy; animal models of human cognitive processes and mental disorders; neurochemical foundations and treatments for mental disorders. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher.
PSYC 462.prerequisiteText: One of PSYC_V 304, PSYC_V 344, PSYC_V 371, BIOL_V 372

PSYC 472.title: Advanced Neuroscience of Motivation
PSYC 472.description: Neurobiological pathways mediating five core aspects of motivated behaviour: (1) affective decision making; (2) motivated drive; (3) goal-directed vs. habit-based behaviour; (4) learning from negative reinforcers; and (5) disorders of motivation. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher.

PSYC 488.title: Directed Studies in Behavioural Neuroscience
PSYC 488.description: Directed investigation of an experimental problem in Behavioural Neuroscience requiring a written report of the findings. Requires the supervising faculty member's permission. See the Department's website for more information. Restricted to Majors in PSYC or COGS or NSCI with third-year standing or higher.

PSYC 498.description: Approved and supervised relevant work experience in an industrial, academic, or government setting for a minimum of 13 weeks, full-time. Normally taken in fourth year Winter Session, Term 2. Work term report required. Pass/Fail. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-op Program in Psychology.
